title: Firewall Breach
premise: A neon cyber-defense arcade game where a glowing core avatar survives waves of hostile intrusion nodes, earns credits, and upgrades weapons between layers.
interaction_model: Touch and pointer drag movement with automatic targeting and firing; between waves the player buys or equips weapons from a shop overlay and manually starts the next wave.
objective: Survive incoming waves, clear each layer of enemies, earn credits from kills, and last as many layers as possible before the core is breached.
progression: Linear run-based wave progression with increasing enemy count, health, and pressure, plus weapon unlocks purchased during between-wave shop phases.
theme: Cyberpunk firewall defense inside an abstract digital grid.
mood: Neon, tense, arcade-forward, synthetic, energetic, and slightly ominous.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy mobile-friendly auto-shooters, arcade survival games, and lightweight wave-based action with simple controls.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is a top-down wave survival shooter with auto-fire and drag movement.
High confidence that the shop is an between-wave weapon progression layer central to the intended loop.
Moderate confidence that the fiction is an abstract cyberspace breach-defense fantasy rather than a literal character-based setting.
recreation_prompt: Recreate a full-screen mobile-friendly HTML5 canvas action game called "Firewall Breach" set inside a glowing cyber grid. The player controls a bright geometric core or security drone in a neon digital arena by dragging anywhere on the screen, with the avatar smoothly following the drag target rather than using buttons. Combat is automatic: the player continuously targets and fires at the nearest enemy whenever a weapon cooldown allows. Enemies are hostile intrusion nodes that spawn from off-screen edges and rush the player in waves, with at least a normal type and a faster variant. Contact damage should chip away at a visible HP bar, while low health and death trigger strong red warning feedback. Each defeated enemy should award credits, show floating reward text, and create punchy particles and hit feedback. Between cleared waves, switch to a shop overlay called a patch bay where the player can buy or equip weapons such as a starter pistol, rapid SMG, rifle, shotgun burst weapon, and a powerful piercing sniper-style gun; then let the player deploy the next harder layer. Presentation should feel sleek and cyberpunk with glowing cyan, magenta, and red accents, a futuristic HUD showing credits, current layer, weapon name, and health, plus animated combat juice like camera shake, impact flashes, success/fail callouts, and state-based music. Structure the run around escalating wave pressure, survival-focused dodging, weapon-based power growth, and a game-over screen that reports how many layers were cleared before the core was breached.
